title: #thelastfiveyears #thelastfiveyearsmusical #thelastfiveyearsbroadway ...
transcript: I saw The Last Five Years and I think I know this score too well for my own good. I always try to stay open-minded with revivals or when shows are in previews, but I have to admit I was pretty skeptical about the casting of Nick Jonas and Adrienne Warren. I'm sorry to report that Nick's vocals didn't do it for me. Apart from the strange ways he places some of his vowels, Nick simply doesn't have the vocal range to climax the songs in the way they're meant to be. He did a lot of opting or riffing out of high, sustained notes, and as an audience member, it's hard to be present when you're nervous if an actor is gonna hit the note. Adrienne sings circles around Nick, but the sound design and sound mixing works more in his favor than hers. Nick's tone works a lot better live and in the space than in the promotional materials. And although Adrienne is giving a more dynamic and impressive vocal performance, something about the way it resonates in the space is making her quieter moments muddy, and I think the sound team is struggling to handle how varied her tone is. As actors, Nick was giving big gestural choices and a pretty clear character arc, whereas Adrienne showed less of an arc but brought more nuance to the delivery of each song, performing them like individual monologues — I found her much more captivating. They have decent chemistry, but they're vocally incompatible — The Next Ten Minutes was rough. Something I liked was the casting of Cathy as a Black woman, which brought an angle to the story I haven't seen before, one where their mutual resentment may be attributed to how Cathy has to work twice as hard to get half as far. But otherwise, the vision and the direction were pretty all over the place, and the blocking felt unnecessarily busy, like there's no reason why The Last Five Years should have a dedicated choreographer. I think if you love this score deeply, you'll need to level your expectations. I'm confident that I would have enjoyed this more with less familiarity to the show. But that's not to say that I didn't enjoy it at all — it still has moments of greatness from both actors, though Adrienne steals the show with her euphorically blazing rendition of I Can Do Better Than That. And if you're a big fan of either performer, this is absolutely worth seeing. With that, other playbill for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer expresses significant disappointment with Nick Jonas's vocals, sound design issues, directional choices, and vocal incompatibility between the leads. While acknowledging some positives (Adrienne Warren's performance, interesting casting choice, moments of greatness), the overall tone is critical with tempered expectations. The recommendation is conditional ('if you're a big fan of either performer') rather than general.
